overview: FlashProve يربط استجابة الاستدلال ببصمة مجموعة أوزان محددة باستخدام zkSNARK دون كشف الأوزان. يركز على Llama 4 Maverick MoE، وهو نموذج بحثي وليس خدمة إنتاجية.

requirements.verifier: Linux x86-64, bash, g++ 13+, Python 3, under 2 GB RAM; build verifier/build.sh then verify stored synthetic example.
requirements.toy: Route 2 additionally requires make and Python 3; approximately 1.5 GB RAM.
requirements.gpuProver: x86-64 Linux, CPU SHA extensions, NVIDIA H100 80 GB, CUDA 13.2 Update 2, gcc/g++ 13, binutils, flock and Python 3.
requirements.fullModel: Llama 4 Maverick route requires Python 3.13, curl, a calibration set, about 245 GB disk, 330 GB host RAM and a 232 GB public 4-bit weight conversion.
requirements.requirementsFileNote: requirements.txt pins PyTorch CUDA 12.8 while the documented prover stack requires CUDA 13.2 Update 2; resolve this mismatch before building.

quickStart: For a safe first look only: clone the repository, read AGENTS.md, build the CPU verifier with verifier/build.sh, then check the stored synthetic example using bin/cp_verify. The toy proof route uses blocks/first_look.sh. No commands were executed in this review.
costModel: No managed service or official price. CPU verifier is relatively light; GPU prover requires H100 time, substantial RAM, storage and power. Cloud use means self-managed H100 rental, not a SaaS offering.
localVsCloud: Verifier and toy route can be explored on a Linux x86-64 machine. Full prover is unsuitable for ordinary laptops and phones. A cloud H100 is technically possible but requires a compatible CUDA environment, 330 GB host RAM for the full model and significant storage.

limitations: The README explicitly says the project is not maintained and is not accepting contributions. The reported evaluation uses a 1,024-token context and an MoE model. Proof generation is costly; the C++ implementation does not carry the same formal guarantee as the Lean specification. No tests or binaries were executed in this review.

improvements.title: Reproducible proof-performance benchmark
improvements.problem: Comparing proof latency, proof size and memory use across setups is difficult.
improvements.approach: Create a harness that records hardware, compiler/CUDA versions, proof time, verification time and artifact size.
steps: Pin the repository commit and environment.
Capture peak memory and proof size.
Attach every result to hardware and version metadata.
improvements.metric: Variance across repeated runs and percentage of reproducible runs.
improvements.risks: H100 rental cost and hardware variation.

improvements.title: Differential tests between Lean and C++ verifiers
improvements.problem: A Lean theorem does not automatically prove that the optimized C++ implementation behaves identically.
improvements.approach: Use fixed vectors and generated edge cases to compare accept/reject decisions.
steps: Create valid and invalid test vectors.
Run both implementations on identical cases.
Review whether the test corpus covers the protocol surface.
improvements.metric: Number of divergent decisions and boundary-case coverage.

improvements.title: Independent verifier package
improvements.problem: Consumers need a narrow parser and reproducible verifier build.
improvements.approach: Package the verification path separately with strict input limits and documented artifacts.
steps: Test missing, malformed and oversized inputs.
improvements.risks: A standalone package can create false confidence without independent audit.

spinoffs.title: Interactive zkML learning lab
spinoffs.problem: Commitments and proofs are difficult to understand from papers alone.
spinoffs.approach: Use a tiny synthetic model to demonstrate commitment, proof generation and CPU verification.
steps: Explain which properties the toy example does not establish.
spinoffs.metric: Completion rate and comprehension of verification outcomes.
spinoffs.risks: Toy examples can understate real-model cost.

spinoffs.title: Inference-model audit ledger
spinoffs.problem: A service user may not know whether the response came from the agreed model weights.
spinoffs.approach: Bind request IDs to a trusted commitment, proof artifact and independent verification result.
spinoffs.metric: Share of requests with valid proofs and verification latency.

spinoffs.title: Comparative research matrix for inference proofs
spinoffs.problem: Results from different papers and prototypes are not directly comparable.
spinoffs.approach: Separate published claims from independently reproduced tests and normalize hardware/context metadata.
steps: Collect FlashProve, VerInf and DeepProve sources.
Extract model, context, hardware and proof assumptions.
Normalize units without mixing incompatible runs.
spinoffs.metric: Share of comparison rows with primary sources and complete conditions.
spinoffs.risks: Metrics may remain incomparable across protocols.
